extracted.intended_audience: corporate crisis communications teams, PR professionals, and executives (CEOs/spokespeople)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting timely, specific, and accountable press releases during a corporate crisis; covers headline/lede/body/quote/boilerplate/contact elements plus behavioral principles and common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Speed matters — first 24 hours determine narrative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue a release within the first 24 hours; the Quality Rubric specifies 'under 24 hours'. Early messaging shapes public narrative and trust; delay risks loss of control and speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity matters — concrete facts and actions; vague statements erode trust
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete facts, timelines, and explicit actions rather than generic statements. Avoid boilerplate like 'we take this seriously' without specifics; show what will be done and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson authority / CEO visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson authority matters — CEO must be visible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the CEO or appropriate executive available and visible in messaging and quotes; 'Make CEO accessible' and 'Spokesperson: CEO visible' are explicit requirements. Avoid hiding behind PR or letting spokespersons obscure executive accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder hierarchy matters — communicate in right order
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and communicate with stakeholders in the correct priority and sequence (e.g., impacted parties first, regulators, employees, then public/media). Ensure commitments to stakeholders are explicit in the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Substance matters — actions, not just statements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on concrete corrective actions, timelines, and accountability rather than abstract assurances. The body and lede should outline what is being done and by whom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathy / human language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes and messaging should lead with empathy before actions; avoid lawyered language or defensive phrasing. Language must sound human and acknowledge harm specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update commitments honored
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify an update schedule in the release and follow it. 'Provide regular updates' is required; failing to honor committed updates undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: state the issue directly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The headline should clearly and directly state the issue. No PR-speak hedging; be straightforward about what happened or what action is being taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: avoid PR-speak hedging
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid passive or evasive phrases in headlines. Do not obscure the issue with marketing language; clarity is paramount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: don't use 'alleged' if facts are clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only qualify with 'alleged' when facts are genuinely uncertain. If facts are established, avoid weakening language that can appear evasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: focus on action
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline — Focus on action being taken
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize immediate remedial or protective actions in the headline when appropriate to signal responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: what happened (concrete facts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with clear, concrete facts about the incident. Avoid speculation and generalities in the lede.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: when it happened (timeline)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include timing in the lead: when the event occurred and any relevant chronology that situates the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: what we're doing (specific actions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State immediate actions being taken in response; be specific rather than vague promises of investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: who's accountable (named individual)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the accountable person or role (e.g., CEO or specific executive) rather than anonymous references to 'management' to demonstrate responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: detailed timeline of events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, detailed chronology in the body so audiences can understand sequence and context. This supports transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: root cause analysis (when known)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report known causes; if the root cause is unknown, state that an investigation is underway and provide expected timelines for findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: specific corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete corrective/remedial steps, who is responsible, and expected completion timelines. Avoid vague 'we will review' statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: independent oversight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, commit to independent investigation or oversight to bolster credibility and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: stakeholder commitments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail commitments to affected stakeholders (e.g., remediation, compensation, monitoring) and how they will be delivered and tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: executive source
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote — From CEO or appropriate executive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a quote from the CEO or relevant senior executive to convey authority and accountability; the quote should be authentic and human.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: empathy first, action second
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure quotes to acknowledge harm and express empathy before describing actions being taken; avoid leading with legal defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: avoid legalese
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep quotes free of lawyered language that can sound evasive or insincere; make quotes relatable and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: be specific, not abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete commitments and references in quotes rather than abstract platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: sound human
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should read/sound like a person speaking: conversational, empathetic, and credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: brief and factual
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the organizational boilerplate concise and factual; do not use it to deflect or defend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: mention crisis-relevant context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contextual information that helps the audience understand the organization's role or capabilities related to the crisis, but avoid defensive phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: avoid defensive language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use boilerplate to shift blame or minimize harm; keep tone factual and accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact — Crisis communications line, 24-hour availability, spokesperson available, update schedule specified
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an explicit crisis line, note 24/7 availability, ensure spokesperson can be reached, and state when the next update will be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid platitudes without specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid lines like 'We take this seriously' without specifics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic statements without detail are listed as pitfalls; pair any such statement with concrete actions and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid minimising apologies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use minimising or dismissive apologies; instead acknowledge harm and take responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not blame victims or third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid blaming victims or third parties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifting blame damages credibility; focus on accountability and remediation instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid lawyered language without empathy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legalistic phrasing that lacks human empathy is a pitfall; combine legal accuracy with human tone where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid going silent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent communication; silence undermines trust. Commit to an update schedule and keep channels active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency across channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure messages are aligned across press releases, social, internal comms, and spokespeople to prevent confusion and erosion of trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid spokesperson hiding behind PR
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let executives hide behind generic PR statements; visible, named leadership is necessary for accountability and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge harm specifically
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe the harm caused (who was affected and how), rather than general expressions of regret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take responsibility clearly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State organizational responsibility where appropriate; be clear about what the organization will do to rectify the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline concrete actions with timelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out specific steps, who will carry them out, and when they will be completed; tie back to update commitments.
